description: Erection of additional storey to Smith House 1 to provide 12 flats and erection of two additional storeys to Smith House 2 to provide 26 flats (overall total: 38 flats), together with associated cycle parking, landscaping, and refuse storage.
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: 
Drawing Numbers:
Drawings E22-028PRP000 (Rev.P3), E22-028PRP001 (Rev.P3), E22-028PRP002 (Rev.P4), E22-028PRP003 (Rev.D), E22-028/PRP004 (Rev.B), E22-028/PRP005 (Rev.B) and E22-028/PRP006 (Rev.P1), received 27/01/2025. Drawing 551-PCA-ZZ-ZZ-DR-L-1001 (Rev.P02a), received 25/11/2024. Drawings E22-028/LOC001 (Rev.P1), E22-028/SIT100 (Rev.F), E22-028/EXE001, E22-028/EXE002, E22-028/EXE003, E22-028/EXE004, E22-028/EXE005, E22-028/PRE001 (Rev.C), E22-028/PRE002 (Rev.B), E22-028/PRE003 (Rev.B), E22-028/PRE004 (Rev.B) and E22-028/PRE005 (Rev.B), received 15/04/2024.
Supporting Documents:
Landscape and urban greening factor document (551-PCA-Landscape text and precedent images), received 10/09/2025. Viability letter (dated 22 May 2025), plus supporting viability information, received 23/05/2025. TM59 Overheating Risk Analysis (5822, 2nd Issue, dated December 2024), received 03/12/2024. Energy Statement (5339, 2nd Issue, dated August 2024), received 09/08/2024. Biodiversity Impact Assessment (P2011.24, dated July 2024), with supporting calculations / details, received 03/07/2024. Car Park Management Plan (PC/P23139 CPMP, 1st Issue, dated March 2024), External Building Fabric Report (14442, Rev.A, dated January 2024), Transport Statement (PC/P23139 TS, 1st Issue, dated March 2024) and Travel Plan (PC/P23139 TP, 1st Issue, dated March 2024), received 16/04/2024. Air Quality Assessment (23-11976, 'FINAL', dated April 2024), Arboricultural Impact Assessment (551.23, Rev.B, dated February 2024), Daylight & Sunlight Assessment (5339, 2nd Issue, dated January 2024), Design Statement (dated April 2024), Fire Statement (Version 1.2, dated 06/04/2024), Schedule of Accommodation SH1, Schedule of Accommodation SH2, Surface and Foul Water Drainage Strategy (AEG3285_TW13_Feltham_07, dated April 2024), and Sustainability Statement (5339, 4th Issue, dated April 2024)
Condition : 3 - No development above ground level shall take place until full details and samples of all materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Details must include a detailed schedule of materials, a photographic sample board and rendered drawings, elevations and sections at a sufficient scale (1:20 or 1:50) to illustrate how all external materials will appear together. The submitted information should cover the following elements:
(a)	Brick/stonework (including brick, stone, masonry, brick panels, feature brick panel, brick framing feature and mortar on-site sample panel, minimum one metre by one metre) including all mortar colours, joint type, brick bond;
(b)	Any cladding materials / render (including specifications);
(c)	Tiles / roof covering; including parapet coping / capping materials, dormers and canopies;
(d)	Window types; and sectional drawings of reveals / courses / sills / textures / head details 
(e)	Balcony details (including soffits, panels and frame);
(f)	All privacy measures (including obscure glazing details, privacy screens etc.);
(g)	Balustrading treatment and handrails to balconies and roof areas (including details / sections / materials); 
(h)	Any other materials/details / fittings to be used (including solar panels, heat pumps, extract vents, rainwater goods, boiler flues etc.), with sections and on-site samples where appropriate.
(h)	Any boundary treatment that may be required
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the conservation area.
Condition : 4 - No external utility boxes (for gas and electricity) shall be affixed to the building and any cables, wires, aerials, pipework, meter boxes or flues shall be discreetly integrated into the building and shall not be fixed to any elevation or roof slope facing a highway. 
No fans, louvres, ducts, water tanks or other external plant shall be installed on the building hereby permitted without the prior written approval of the local planning authority. 
No advertisements shall be displayed on the development without details of the advertisements having first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Council through securing of Advertisement Consent and/or Planning Permission. 
Reason: In order to safeguard the visual amenity of the area and neighbours living conditions.
Condition : 5 - Notwithstanding any details included in the submitted plans, no development above ground level shall take place until full and finalised details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include:  
- a statement setting out the design objectives and how these will be delivered; 
- an implementation programme (including phasing of work where relevant); 
- plans and written specifications of all soft landscaping works, including any grass and turf areas, trees, planters, shrub and herbaceous areas, noting details of species, sizes, numbers / densities and any associated cultivation / relevant operations;
- a 'Tree Planting Statement' providing full details, numbers, locations, specifications and construction / planting methods for all purpose-built tree pits and associated above ground features, including specifications for tree protection and a stated volume of suitable growing medium to facilitate and promote the healthy development of the proposed trees, ensuring each tree has a soil volume equivalent of 0.6 times its canopy area at maturity. Also demonstrating compliance with the Manual for Streets and compatibility with any existing paving and underground utilities infrastructure;
- existing and proposed finished levels or contours; 
- proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (e.g. drainage, power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating alignments, levels, access points/manholes, supports as relevant); 
- hard landscaping proposals, including ground surface materials, kerbs, edges, ridge and flexible paving, refuse disposal points and if applicable synthetic surfaces for both ground level and roof terrace level (where relevant); 
- renewable energy installations (including solar PVs and air source heat pumps with details of any associated screening/noise insulation);
- fences, walls and any other boundary treatments/retaining 
Condition : 6 - Prior to commencement of any above ground works associated with the development, full details of the proposed green roof elements shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, including planting schedules (sizes; numbers/densities; species etc.) and maintenance and management arrangements, and taking account of drainage and surface water runoff, access to natural light / sunlight and growth potential. Details shall include: 
(i)	Construction drawings to include a plan, cross sections; 
(ii)	Native wildflower seed mix (turf or sedum blanket will not be accepted); 
(iii)	Substrate between 80mm-150mm in depth; undulating and contain different materials/sizes (sand, gravel, crushed ceramic, brick, recycled, inert materials); 
(iv)	Small piles of untreated logs; 
(v)	Confirmation that no irrigation will be used; 
(vi)	Confirmation that the green roof construction will be supervised by a suitable qualified landscape/ecology contractor;
(vii) 	Provisions for appropriate mitigation should green features decline. 
The approved details shall be implemented in full prior to occupation and shall be retained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interests of biodiversity and ensuring a satisfactory appearance of the site and wider conservation area.
Condition : 7 - Prior to first occupation of the development, details (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the following sustainable sourcing of materials requirements:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- 	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme. 
- 	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.
Condition : 8 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the hereby approved Energy Statement (5339, 2nd Issue, dated August 2024), Sustainability Statement (5339, 4th Issue, dated April 2024) and TM59 Overheating Risk Analysis (5822, 2nd Issue, dated December 2024) documents. 
b)	Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that these areas of development have been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement to achieve a site-wide carbon reduction in emissions of at least 82% on Part L Building Regulations. 
c)	Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, suitable devices for the monitoring of the low and zero carbon technologies shall have been installed, and the monitored data shall be submitted automatically to a monitoring web-platform at daily intervals for a period of three years from the point of full operation.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 9 - Prior to first occupation of the development, full details of the proposed heat pumps shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These shall include:
-	An estimate of the heating and/or cooling energy (MWh/annum) the heat pumps would provide to the development and the percentage of contribution to the site's heat loads to demonstrate how the heat fraction from heat pump technologies has been maximised.
-	Details of the Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) and/or Seasonal Energy Efficiency ratio (SEER) and how these have been calculated including the expected heat source and heat distribution temperatures (for space heat and hot water) and the distribution loss factor, which shall be calculated based on the above information.
-	Details of all screening and acoustic insulation to protect against visual harm and undue noise and disturbance to surrounding sensitive receptors. 
The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the air source heat pumps hereby approved shall generate no more than 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, during all times that the mechanical system is in operation. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive uses or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive uses, and in accordance with the latest British Standard 4142 (or any successor to this). An alternative position for assessment / measurement may be used to allow ease of access; however, this must first be agreed in writing by the local planning authority and illustrated on a map with noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria is achieved.
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards, to protect residents living conditions and to preserve the amenities of the area.
Condition : 10 - Prior to commencement of any above-ground works on the development hereby permitted (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), details of the specifications regarding power, number, appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority to show how the renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved and maximised. The photovoltaic panels shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the relevant part of the development and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards and to ensure the development does not endanger the safe movement of aircraft or the operation of Heathrow Airport. The airport requires a glint and glare assessment to be completed to determine the full impact on pilots approaching the airport.
Condition : 11 - No development shall take place until a preliminary non-intrusive risk assessment (Phase I desk study report) to identify possible areas and sources of land contamination which may exist on the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. It will establish what intrusive investigation or site remediation measures may be necessary before the development commences. This report will be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes: 
(i) The Phase I desk study report will include the aims and objectives, data collection, site reconnaissance (walk over survey) and development of the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) with preliminary risk assessment whereby risk of all potential pollutant linkages are evaluated with a risk category. 
(ii) The report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii) The report shall also make recommendations for the further gathering of information and/or intrusive investigation, to ensure that it will be possible to render the site safe for its proposed use.
(iv) The Council requests that the risk assessment reports or site plans are sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 12 - Following the completion of the Phase I desk study report, if intrusive investigations or gas monitoring is recommended, a Phase II site investigation must be undertaken especially at the proposed landscaping areas. 
No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. 
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work. 
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the Local Planning Authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where it is deemed necessary to secure ade
Condition : 13 - If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development (except refurbishment of existing buildings, demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the Local Planning Authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 14 - The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. 
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the Local Planning Authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 15 - The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented as part of the development. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation for relevant parts of the development by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval, before that part of the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 16 - If long-term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the Local Planning Authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice. 
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. 
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.
Condition : 17 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein. 
The developer shall keep an up-to-date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/. 
Reason: In the interests of preventing harmful air quality impacts.
Condition : 18 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a finalised and detailed Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CEMP shall provide details of how demolition and construction works are to be undertaken and include:
-	An identification of stages of works (including site preparation and construction stages); 
-	Procedures for maintaining good public relations including complaint management (logbook for complaints), public consultation and liaison, all in compliance with British Standards BS 5228-1:2009+A1:2014 and best practicable means;
-	Mitigation measured as defined in BS 5228: Parts 1 and 2: 2009 Noise and Vibration Control on Construction and Open Sites shall be used to minimise noise disturbance from construction works (including noise mitigation measures for all plant and processors);
-	Measures to control emissions (including dust suppression and the need to contain stored or accumulated material so as to prevent it becoming airborne at any time) during the construction phase, in line with the requirements of the Mayor's Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, including the methods to be used and the measures to be undertaken to monitor and control the emission of dust, noise and vibration arising from construction works;
-	Details showing how all vehicles associated with the construction works are properly washed and cleaned to prevent the passage to mud and dirt onto the adjoining highway);
-	Details of provisions for recycling of materials, the provision on site of a storage/delivery area for all plant, site huts, site facilities and materials;
-	Details of a community liaison contact for the duration of all works associated with the development;
-	Any asbestos survey to be carried out; and
-	Any mobile crusher to be used on site (if required), including 
Condition : 19 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am to 6:00pm on Mondays to Friday and 8:00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority. Additionally, HGV deliveries to the site during the course of construction will be restricted to between 9:30am and 3:00pm on Mondays to Fridays, and between 9:30am and 1:00pm on Saturdays, and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of the locality and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the public highway.
Condition : 20 - No development shall take place, (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) that conforms to current TfL and CLOCS guidance has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The Plan shall include: 
i.	a site plan (showing the areas set out below);
ii.	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage to the adjoining public highway which has been caused directly by the development hereby permitted (including demolition and construction phases); 
iii.	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors, and any interim car parking measures that might be necessary during the construction period;
iv.	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
v.	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
vi.	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network (including hours of access, access and egress arrangements within the site and security procedures);
vii.	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate, and clear contact details of the site manager;
viii.	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
ix.	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works;
x.	measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;
xi.	comm
Condition : 21 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 22 - Secure covered cycle parking facilities (minimum 69 additional long-stay spaces and 2 visitor spaces) for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be installed in the locations specified on Drawing 551-PCA-ZZ-ZZ-DR-L-1001 (Rev.P02a). The approved facilities shall conform to the current London Plan Cycle Parking Guidance (or such other guidance as shall supersede it) in design and layout and be fully implemented and made available for use before the first occupation of the development or commencement of the approved use as appropriate and thereafter retained for use alongside the 138 cycle parking facilities for the rest of the existing residential units at Smith House at all times without obstruction. 
Reason: To support sustainable transport objectives. 
Condition : 23 - At least three months before completion of the development hereby approved, full and finalised details of the ecological enhancement, urban greening factor and habitat improvement measures to be adopted shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submitted information shall show how the anticipated urban greening factor and biodiversity net gain scores set out in the approved Biodiversity Impact Assessment (P2011.24, dated July 2024) and supporting calculations / details and Landscape and urban greening factor document are to be delivered and achieved on site (and where possible exceeded), with details provided explaining how the enhancement/landscaping measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long- term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules. Details of any bird and bat boxes and other viable ecological enhancements (e.g. nest boxes / bricks/ cups; insect blocks; reptile log piles; hedgehog houses etc.) shall be provided, alongside full details of any lighting proposed to show how this would be designed and positioned to minimise impacts on new planting and habitats being created.  
The scheme as approved shall then be implemented prior to first occupation of any part of the development and shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details. Any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the local planning authority.
Development shall also be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment (551.23, Rev.B, dated February 2024) hereby approved, with all protection measures put in place and retained for the duration of the development to ensure that all trees at the site and within its vicinity would be protected.
Reason: In the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity. 
Condition : 24 - The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO). Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence of the accreditation achieved shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: To minimise opportunities for crime and to increase safety for residents and people in the locality.
Condition : 25 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of any noise (LAeq) emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), along with any heat pumps or mechanical gates or other mechanical infrastructure to which this permission refers, shall remain at least 10dB(A) below the existing representative background noise level (LA90) at all times that the plant operates. 
The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance with the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/ measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved.
b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter. 
c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant described in part (a) of this condition, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the Local Planning Authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again. This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the requir
Condition : 26 - (a) Development shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations of the External Building Fabric Report (14442-EBF-02_RevA, dated January 2024) hereby approved, ensuring that noise levels within the dwellings and external amenity areas do not exceed those that are specified in Table 4 of British Standard 8233:2014 or equivalent standards if replaced.
(b) Prior to the development being occupied, sound insulation test reports demonstrating compliance with the scheme approved under Part A of this condition, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Noise tests shall be carried out taking account of worst-case environmental conditions, such as easterly operations at Heathrow, peak time traffic flows wind speed, direction and presence of temperature inversion. Continuous logged data shall be submitted.
Reason: In order to secure acceptable living conditions for residential occupiers of the new care home and protect the living conditions of surrounding residents. 
Condition : 27 - Prior to first occupation of the development, a finalised Fire Statement shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which includes: details of a suitable water supply and proof that all relevant fire hydrants are operable; green roof fire safety measures; evidence that solar PV panel cabling would be suitably supported to avoid obstruction of escape routes and firefighting access due to failure of fixings; details of an appropriate signage system and colour coding for the fire-fighting stair design; details of evacuation lifts (with enhanced repair services running 365 days/24-hour cover to ensure no wheelchair occupiers are trapped if a lift breaks down); confirmation that all external doors to the premises would be fitted with self-closing devices and maintained in an operational condition; and proof that power supplies, electrical wiring and control equipment would have appropriate levels of protection against fire.  Development shall be carried out in accordance with this finalised Statement.
Reason: To ensure appropriate measures in place in the interest of fire safety.
Condition : 28 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order) no change of use, enlargement of the premises or provision of additional structures/buildings within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: In the interests of the amenity of the area and order not that the Local Planning Authority is able to exercise control over future development of the site.
